stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PHvP Prefer DW on Google The average human brain consumes about 20% of the body's energy despite making up only around 2% of its weight. Image: Irina Romanova/Zoonar/picture alliance Advertisement You know when you lock your phone and the screen goes black? It seems like it's not doing anything. But it's not doing nothing. It's syncing your messages, updating apps and running other background processes. Your brain has its own version of that. Imagine you're sitting on a bus, staring out of a window, taking a shower or walking, and you get that feeling of doing nothing and letting your mind drift? Well, your mind, the brain, is doing a lot when it feels like you're doing nothing. It's going over your memories, shaping your sense of who you are, imagining possible futures, helping you understand other people and connecting ideas. That's your brain's default mode network. stories.summary: Women who scored high on intelligence tests were seen as more hostile by their teammates and got less help, a new study finds. High-scoring men faced no such penalty. Research explains why.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PITB Prefer DW on Google Image: DW Advertisement High intelligence is usually counted as an asset at work.
